reasons: The full text is pinned and hash-verified in a community mirror.
The control number, contest year, problem, and Outstanding Winner label match a COMAP official result PDF.
The paper itself is not served from an official paper-display page, so the level is B rather than A.

page_evidence.observation: The paper begins with title and contents but no standalone abstract.
The US transplant network is represented as a rooted tree and discrete-time process.
Base-model objectives and assumptions are stated beside the first results.
A full process flowchart exposes patient, organ, matching, operation, failure, and death transitions.
Policy scenarios are compared through aligned outcome curves.
A parameter sweep shows the effect of an allocation parameter on outcomes.
Strengths and weaknesses cover flexibility, ethics, data manipulation, and computational cost.

abstract_structure.observation: No result-bearing abstract is present; the contents reveal coverage but not recommendations or quantitative results.

model_chain.observation: Represent the transplant system as a rooted tree with time-dependent patient and organ arrivals.
Simulate priority matching, operations, failure, survival, and death updates.
Apply alternative-country policies and kidney-exchange rules within the same simulator.
Add patient choice and ethical or political decision effects.

validation_chain.observation: Quantify the base allocation model under explicit assumptions.
Compare outcome curves for alternative policies.
Sweep a decision parameter and inspect outcome stability.
Separate computational, data, ethical, and policy limitations.

figures.lesson: Make state transitions and feedback loops visible before policy variants.
Use repeated axes to compare transplant outcomes across policies.
Show how a policy parameter changes the outcome before recommending it.

code_links.note: No independently packaged source tree was paired with this exact PDF; embedded appendix fragments are not treated as reproducible code.

transferable_rules.rule: For discrete-event policy models, draw the complete state-transition loop before equations.
Evaluate policy variants inside one common simulator and common output contract.
Treat ethical scope limits separately from numerical-model weaknesses.

risks.risk: Missing abstract delays access to the decision and result.
The model's flexibility permits data manipulation and raises computational cost, as the authors acknowledge.
Several line plots use very small legends and labels.

provenance.review_method: full-page render overview plus 4-7 high-resolution evidence-page visual checks and extracted-text review
